column3: NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “having called a child.”
Close to the Greek; “turn” is rendered “are converted.”
Close to the Greek; “causes to stumble” is rendered “causes to sin,” and “sunk” as “drowned.”
Close to the Greek; “causes of sin” is rendered “offenses.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV reverses “crippled or lame” to “lame or maimed.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (“the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost”).
NKJV has “leave the ninety-nine and go to the mountains,” following the Textus Receptus wording; the critical text reads “leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go.”
Close to the Greek; “reprove him” is rendered “tell him his fault.”
Close to the Greek; “the pagan” is rendered “a heathen.”
NKJV has “Again I say,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Again, amen I say.”
NKJV has “seventy times seven”; the Greek ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά may also mean “seventy-seven times.”
NKJV includes “Master,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins the plea with “Have patience.”
NKJV includes “at his feet” and “all,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “fell down … I will pay you.”
